# MPkWh.com

> MPkWh.com ranks the most efficient electric cars available in the US by miles per kWh (Mi/kWh) — the EV equivalent of MPG. Data is sourced from official EPA fuel economy ratings and updated weekly every Monday.

## What is Mi/kWh?

Miles per kilowatt-hour (Mi/kWh) measures how far an electric vehicle travels on one unit of electricity. A higher number means greater efficiency: lower energy consumption, lower running costs, and longer range from the same battery. Mi/kWh is calculated as EPA-rated range divided by usable battery capacity — the portion of the pack the car can actually access. This measures battery-to-wheel efficiency.

## Notes

- Mi/kWh = EPA range ÷ usable battery capacity. Measures battery-to-wheel efficiency (not wall-to-wheel, which would include charging losses).
- Efficiency figures reflect the most efficient trim and configuration available for each model year.
- Pack sizes sourced from ev-database.org, manufacturer spec pages, and EPA energy calculations (range × kWh/100mi × 0.89 charging efficiency). Tesla does not publicly disclose battery capacity — Tesla usable kWh figures are cross-verified via EPA energy data and C&D spec boxes.
- Not all 2026 models have received EPA ratings yet. The table is updated every Monday as new ratings are published.
- Cost-per-100-miles uses the latest US average residential electricity rate published monthly by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA). As of October 2026: $0.1816/kWh (August 2026 figure, published October 2026).
- Data source: US EPA fueleconomy.gov, ev-database.org

## Break-Even MPG

Break-even MPG is the gasoline fuel economy at which a car's monthly gasoline spending exactly equals an electric car's monthly payment plus its electricity cost. A gas vehicle rated below the break-even figure spends enough on fuel that the avoided spending would cover the EV.

break_even_mpg = monthly_miles × gas_price_per_gallon ÷ (ev_monthly_payment + ev_electricity_cost)

The EV's electricity cost is monthly miles ÷ Mi/kWh, increased by a charging overhead (15% by default, because Mi/kWh measures battery-to-wheel efficiency rather than the energy drawn from the wall), multiplied by the residential electricity rate.

This is a fuel-and-electricity comparison only. It excludes insurance, registration, sales and use tax, maintenance, depreciation, financing opportunity cost, parking, and home charger installation. "Fuel savings cover the payment" means avoided gasoline spending is equal to or greater than the EV's payment plus electricity — not that total ownership cost is zero.

Break-even MPG is highly sensitive to annual mileage and to local gasoline prices. At low mileage and low gasoline prices it falls into single digits, where essentially no production vehicle qualifies; at high mileage or high regional prices it rises into full-size truck and SUV territory.

## Pages

- [Home](https://mpkwh.com/): Full ranked table with EPA range, pack kWh, usable kWh, Mi/kWh, and cost-per-100-miles for all models.
- [Break-even calculator](https://mpkwh.com/break-even/): Interactive calculator showing what share of an EV's monthly payment a gas car's avoided fuel spending would cover, plus the break-even MPG threshold. All inputs editable.
